page: UpCloud PREMIUM-1xCPU-2GB is an entry-level virtual server configuration within the Premium family, deployed via KVM virtualization. The instance features a single shared vCPU based on the AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture. It includes 2.0 GB of RAM, a 25 GB local SSD storage volume, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server operates without dedicated hardware GPU accelerators. The CPU provides advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX512-BF16, AES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded instruction execution despite the entry-level footprint. The stress-ng single-core score of 3810.08, along with single-threaded gzip compression at 39.69 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.35 GB/sec, places single-core throughput in the top tier. However, overall multi-core aggregate throughput remains limited by the single-core allocation, reflected in low overall PassMark CPU scores and bottom-quartile multi-core stress-ng metrics. Read-only small-block memory bandwidth measures 184.03 GB/sec, while uncached large-block write bandwidth reaches an average 30.46 GB/sec.

Because it features a shared 1 vCPU allocation paired with 2 GB of system memory, the instance presents an economical entry point for lightweight services rather than high-density compute clusters. The trade-off centers on the shared core topology: while single-threaded tasks exploit modern Zen-based vector instructions effectively, overall memory bandwidth and aggregate operations per second remain constrained, as indicated by bottom-tier PassMark database operations and Redis SET performance.

The hardware profile fits low-volume web serving, lightweight automation scripts, edge proxying, small background workers, and staging environments. Workloads requiring sustained multi-threading, massive memory capacity, or heavy concurrent database transactions will encounter constraints given the single-core shared topology and 2.0 GB memory envelope.
